questions.stem: On a pleasure craft, which flotation may each person have to meet the law?
options: A SOLAS lifejacket and nothing else
A lifejacket or an approved PFD
A floating seat cushion of any kind
A PFD, but only for the children
questions.explanation: On a pleasure craft either a lifejacket or an approved PFD of the right size is allowed for each person.

questions.stem: When does a pleasure craft need a reboarding device such as a ladder?
options: When the climb is over 0.5 m
Only if it has a swim grid
questions.explanation: A reboarding device is needed unless the climb back on board from the water is 0.5 m or less.

questions.stem: A 5 m runabout must carry a buoyant heaving line. How long must it be?
questions.explanation: Up to 6 m, the boat needs a buoyant heaving line of at least 15 m.

questions.stem: What visual signals must a 5.5 m outboard boat carry on the ocean?
questions.explanation: Up to 6 m: a watertight flashlight or three approved pyrotechnic distress signals.

questions.stem: A 7.5 m cabin boat runs in Haro Strait. What visual signals must it carry?
questions.explanation: Over 6 m and up to 9 m: a watertight flashlight and six flares, no more than two of them smoke signals.

questions.stem: What may a 5 m runabout carry instead of an anchor with 15 m of line?
questions.explanation: Up to 9 m the boat carries an anchor with at least 15 m of rode, or a manual propelling device such as a paddle or oars, plus a bailer or manual pump.

questions.stem: Your 5 m boat is only ever used in daylight and good visibility. Must it carry navigation lights?
questions.explanation: Up to 9 m, navigation lights are needed only if the boat is out between sunset and sunrise or in poor visibility.

questions.stem: When does a 6 m powerboat NOT need to carry flares?
options: On a lake never over 1 nm from shore
On any trip shorter than two hours
On the open ocean during summer
Whenever the sky is clear and bright
questions.explanation: Flares are not required on a river, canal or lake where the boat can never be more than 1 nautical mile from shore.

questions.stem: How long after the date of manufacture do pyrotechnic flares expire?
questions.explanation: Flares expire 4 years after they were made. The date is stamped on each one.

questions.stem: Which person may use an inflatable PFD as their required flotation?
options: An adult on a personal watercraft
An adult who wears it on deck
A child of 9 in a canoe
questions.explanation: Inflatable PFDs are not allowed for anyone under 16 or on a PWC, and they must be worn to count.

questions.stem: What kind of flotation device must a 12-year-old wear on your boat?
questions.explanation: The regulations say flotation worn by anyone under 16 must be inherently buoyant, so inflatables are out.

questions.stem: How often should you check your lifejackets and PFDs for rips, fading and broken straps?
questions.explanation: Transport Canada advises checking them at least once a year, and replacing any that are damaged.

questions.stem: A 5.5 m runabout has an outboard with a portable tank, no stove and no inboard engine. Must it carry a fire extinguisher?
questions.explanation: Up to 6 m, a 5B:C extinguisher is required only with an inboard engine, a fixed fuel tank or a fuel-burning appliance. Carrying one is still wise.
